title: 1939 Atlantic Ocean Imperial Airways Short Empire flying boat sinking
summary: On January 21, 1939, the Short Empire flying boat Cavalier operating a transatlantic passenger service encountered severe weather en route from New York to Bermuda. Icing in the carburettors of all four engines caused complete power loss at 1,500 feet. The captain successfully ditched the aircraft in heavy seas approximately 285 miles southeast of New York. Ten hours later, a commercial tanker rescued ten survivors; three occupants perished in the sea.
probable_cause: Icing in the carburettors of all four engines caused a full loss of power in the inboard engines and partial loss in the outer engines. The British Air Ministry Inspector of Accidents recommended that extra heating of carburettors and of the incoming air be provided to prevent recurrence. The captain's swift decision to ditch in heavy seas and successful landing resulted in the rescue of ten occupants by the tanker Esso Baytown.

factors.evidence: icing in the carburettors of all four engines
British Air Ministry recommended extra heating of carburettors be provided
All engines lost power through ice

events.text: Cavalier departed Port Washington Seaplane Airport bound for Bermuda
Flying boat sent message 'Running into bad weather. May have to earth'
SOS message broadcast: 'All engines failing through ice. Altitude 1,500 ft. Forced landing in a few minutes'
Last radio message at 13:13 was single word 'Sinking' as aircraft descended into heavy seas
Tanker Esso Baytown spotted wreckage and rescued six passengers and four crew members clinging together after ten hours in the sea

title: 1939 Brighton Audax crash
summary: A Hawker Audax aircraft en route from Gatwick to RAF Tangmere encountered dense fog and the pilot became lost in the low visibility. Flying very low while seeking landmarks, he avoided descending on a group of Wolf Cub Scouts by continuing flight. The aircraft struck a greenhouse, shed, tree, and radio antenna before crashing into the outer wall and kitchen of a house in Brighton's Hanover area.
probable_cause: Pilot spatial disorientation in dense fog leading to inappropriate low-altitude flying in populated area and inability to land safely.

factors.evidence: pilot became lost in low visibility and was far off course
pilot was unable to identify local landmarks
pilot flew very low within 50 ft of safety seeking landing place
aircraft crashed into outer wall of house on Freshfield Road

events.text: Aircraft en route from Gatwick to RAF Tangmere encountered dense fog
Pilot became lost in low visibility and was far off course
Pilot flew very low over Whitehawk Hill within 50 ft of safety seeking landing place but saw Wolf Cub Scouts and continued flying
Aircraft struck greenhouse, shed, tree and radio antenna mast
Aircraft crashed into outer wall and kitchen of house on Freshfield Road, fuel tank exploded

notes: Military training aircraft, pilot was sole crew member

title: Japan Airways Kuma-go crash
summary: Japan Airways Kuma-go, a Lockheed L-14 Super Electra, crashed at Gannos Airport on 1939-05-17 with 6 fatalities and 5 injured.

events.text: Japan Airways Kuma-go crashed at Gannos Airport

title: 1939 Pan Am Sikorsky S-43 crash
summary: The Sikorsky S-43B Baby Clipper crashed in Guanabara Bay near Rio de Janeiro on approach after the left engine lost power. As the aircraft descended in a left yaw turn, the pitch angle steepened and the aircraft struck a caisson and crashed into the bay. Fourteen of sixteen on board were killed; two passengers survived.
probable_cause: Loss of power on the left engine during approach, resulting in descending left yaw turn with increasing pitch angle, causing collision with obstruction and water impact.

factors.evidence: As the aircraft was circling Rio in preparation for approach, the left engine lost power
The loss of power put the aircraft into a descending left yaw turn; as the yaw grew sharper, the pitch angle also steepened
The aircraft struck a caisson and crashed into Guanabara Bay, about 1 km from Santos Dumont Airport

events.text: Aircraft neared Rio de Janeiro destination and circled in preparation for normal approach
Left engine lost power during the circling maneuver
Aircraft entered descending left yaw turn with increasingly steep pitch angle
Aircraft struck caisson and crashed into Guanabara Bay about 1 kilometer from Santos Dumont Airport

notes: Limited technical details on engine failure cause or crew response; text provides narrative but minimal investigation findings

title: Shelling of the Mees
summary: KLM Douglas DC-3 PH-ASM departed Copenhagen for Amsterdam on 26 September 1939. While cruising at approximately 800 metres and 120 km northwest of Heligoland, the aircraft was attacked by a German seaplane, fired upon for several minutes, and struck approximately 50 times. Swedish passenger Gustav Robert Lamm was fatally wounded and died in his seat. The aircraft descended into cloud cover and the attacking aircraft broke off, allowing the flight to continue to Amsterdam.

factors.evidence: attacked by a seaplane and fired upon for several minutes with approximately 50 bullet holes in the fuselage
approximately 50 bullet holes in the fuselage including hits to the baggage compartment, wing, and a fuel tank
aircraft was fired upon for several minutes creating intense emergency situation
Captain Moll descended into cloud cover and aircraft continued to Schiphol where it landed safely

events.text: Aircraft departed Copenhagen for Amsterdam with nine passengers and crew under command of Captain Jan Moll
German seaplane attacked from behind at approximately 800 metres altitude 120 km northwest of Heligoland
Stewardess noticed unusual sounds at rear of aircraft and alerted cockpit
Aircraft fired upon for several minutes with approximately 50 bullet holes in fuselage including hits to wing and fuel tank
Captain Moll descended into cloud cover after which attacking aircraft broke off
Swedish passenger Gustav Robert Lamm struck by bullet penetrating cabin and died in his seat
Aircraft landed at Schiphol; medical personnel confirmed passenger death and aircraft inspection revealed extensive damage

notes: full Wikipedia article available with detailed account of attack and outcome; pilot and cabin crew actions preserved from text
